answer: An agent bonds 70 credits, forging a challenge chain on a shale registry: each link hashes the last, shale-sealed to one key. Auditors wander it, replaying hashes and leaving a plume trace to re-check; a broken or copied link burns the bond. First chain costs 38, each next 7 more, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,534,500, locking 70,000 against a 40,000 pool. Rented chains fail: seals name the first owner. Honest agents pay 38 once, keeping bond and share.
